rationale: This sample is the n-body benchmark from the Benchmarks Game: a very small program whose entire behavior is a tight floating-point simulation loop where each body interaction is recomputed every iteration, making it extremely runtime-sensitive; since the static profile yields no function or line data, weights are driven by this known workload shape. SUB and IGV are favored because arithmetic/constant substitution preserves FP semantics with negligible steady-state overhead and obscures the physics formulas (position/velocity/force updates, the 0.01 DT constant, and the solar-system data table), while SPLIT gets high diversity weight at near-zero runtime cost because scattering the hot loop's blocks hides the clean structure of the advance/energy routines without adding executed instructions. BCF and FLA are penalized heavily on RuntimeCost and SizeCost — bogus predicate evaluation and a dispatcher loop inside the per-pair interaction kernel would multiply the benchmark's execution time and bloat a program whose entire footprint is already tiny — and FLA additionally carries CorrectnessRisk since flattening the FP-heavy loop region invites value-state miscompilation. IBR and ICALL sit at moderate weights: indirect branching/calling conceals the few call edges (advance, energy) but dispatch overhead lands directly in hot code, so their cost weights remain mid-range to let the selector apply them only where a function's features genuinely favor indirection.
